title: A raising constant operand fails the plan whatever guards it
verdict: a pure-constant operand is evaluated at plan resolution, guard or not
description: A `when/then` branch that is a pure-constant expression and raises is evaluated while the plan is resolved, whatever the condition is: `pl.LazyFrame({"x": [-1, -2]}).select(pl.when(pl.col("x") > 0).then(pl.lit(300).cast(pl.Int8, strict=True))).collect(engine="streaming")` raises `InvalidOperationError` (conversion from `i128` to `i8` failed in column 'scalar') on rows where the condition is FALSE, and so does `pl.lit('bad').cast(pl.Int64, strict=True) > 0` under a literal-FALSE, a column and a data-FALSE reach. `optimizations=pl.QueryOptFlags.none()` changes nothing. A branch that reads a column is evaluated lazily (polars-guarded-column-lazy).

Sverify's checker folds a constant error without regard to its guard and refuses or reports it (a cast of `'bad'` or of 300 to TINYINT is refused; `1 // 0`, `sqrt(-1.0)`, `ln(0.0)`, overflow and `abs` of the minimum give `unproved` with the error, also under a precondition that makes the branch unreachable), so a plan with a raising constant is never certified raise-free (D21, ruling 100).
reference: `CASE WHEN r THEN k END` with a raising constant `k` raises only where `r` holds; D21 fails every plan with a raising constant, so a verified plan never carries one.

evidence.note: `python -m sverify_dev.guarded_columns p1 --engine polars`: Polars 2.1.0 (Python), streaming engine, Linux x86_64 (homelab); the P1 cases also ran on macOS arm64 for DuckDB and Polars with the same result.

provenance.notes: Issue #1719 (D50-d). Probe rows: 3000, every third one the text `bad`, which a strict cast rejects.
